meta.title: Pricing in 2027: raise where customers stay, test where they compare
meta.subtitle: Should Palisade raise prices while churn is rising? Discussion document for the CEO and leadership team
meta.purpose: Should Palisade raise prices at its 2027 renewals while churn is rising, and if so where and by how much, to grow ARR at least 15% with NRR above 100%?
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data: the company and all figures are fictional

inputs.label: Planning choices made on the team's behalf (user unavailable)
inputs.content: Choices made on the leadership team's behalf because the user was unavailable: mode deck_deep (CEO decision); material = briefing pack only, no web; audience CEO and leadership team approving the 2027 plan; theme navy; deck type client diagnostic, 30-40 slides; issue tree cut by the conditions of the decision. Planning choices: Mid-market: +10% at 2027 renewals (the level tested in 2024). Enterprise: +10% at 2027 renewals where uncapped; contract cap of 7% where capped. SMB: list price held; +8% test on a random half of non-promotion renewals, January to March 2027. Sensitivity settings for 2027: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5 and 3.0 times the 2023 response.

storyline.governing_thought: Raise prices on mid-market and enterprise renewals in 2027; hold SMB prices until a test shows a rise is safe

exec_summary.text: Rising churn comes from the 2025 promotion cohort, not from a reaction to list prices

sub_points.text: Win rate in SMB deals with Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year
A 12% rise stops paying at twice the 2023 churn response

exec_summary.text: A segmented rise adds about $4.3M and can reach 15% growth with little new business

Only $0.6M of new ARR is needed; NRR rises to about 114%

problem.statement: Should Palisade raise prices at its 2027 renewals while churn is rising, and if so where and by how much, to grow ARR at least 15% with NRR above 100%?
problem.decision_maker: CEO and leadership team, approving the 2027 pricing plan
success_criteria: ARR grows at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M
Net revenue retention stays above 100% overall
Price changes respect renewal dates and enterprise contract terms
problem.accuracy: Directional: ARR effects to within about $1M, from the briefing pack only

one_day_answer.situation: Palisade has $86.0M of ARR in three segments; SMB monthly churn rose from 2.0% to 3.1%, and the CFO proposes 12% on every plan
one_day_answer.complication: The CEO fears a rise will push churn higher, Inkwell now sells a $9 SMB plan, and nobody has split churn by cohort
one_day_answer.resolution: Raise prices where customers stay for integrations and audit trail, hold SMB until a test proves it safe, and treat the promotion cohort as an activation problem

issue_tree.label: Churn
issue_tree.hypothesis: Rising churn comes from the 2025 promotion cohort, not from customers reacting to the list price
The rise in churn is concentrated in the customers the 2025 promotion brought in

workplan.analysis: Split the rise in customers lost per month by segment and cohort
workplan.exhibit: waterfall-bridge; bar-ranking of churn by group

finding.note: About 90% of the rise in customers lost per month comes from the promotion cohort; other SMB churn moved 2.0% to 2.1%

issue_tree.hypothesis: Promotion customers leave because they never set the product up, not because of the list price

workplan.analysis: First-month activation by cohort; exit-survey price reasons by group

finding.note: Low activation (41% against 72%) and the end of the 50% discount together: 52% cite price, most left within two months of the discount ending

issue_tree.hypothesis: An onboarding programme will halve SMB churn within two quarters

workplan.analysis: Best case if every promotion customer churned like the rest, against the promised level

finding.note: Fixing the promotion cohort cuts SMB churn by about a third (3.1% to 2.1%); halving would also need other SMB churn below its pre-2023 1.8% within two quarters

issue_tree.label: Larger customers
issue_tree.hypothesis: Mid-market and enterprise customers will accept a 2027 price rise without leaving
Mid-market buyers do not react to a 10% higher list price

finding.note: 23.1% against 23.6%, not significant; covers new sign-ups only, not renewals

issue_tree.hypothesis: Larger customers stay for integrations and audit trail, where Inkwell does not compete

workplan.analysis: Retention drivers, Inkwell's deal footprint, segment NRR

finding.note: Advisory board names integrations and audit trail; Inkwell not seen above 200 seats; NRR 112% and 118%

issue_tree.hypothesis: Mid-market churn is stable, so a rise starts from a steady base

finding.note: Churn rose from 0.6% to 0.8% a month for unknown reasons; the rise needs a renewal control group

issue_tree.label: SMB
issue_tree.hypothesis: SMB customers will accept a 2027 list-price rise without a costly rise in churn
SMB churn returns to normal soon after a price rise, as it did in 2023

workplan.analysis: 2023 churn path; scale to a 12% rise

finding.note: Churn spiked for six months and settled higher; scaled to 12%, the rise keeps only about half of its $2.5M

issue_tree.hypothesis: Inkwell has made SMB buyers more price-sensitive

workplan.analysis: Price ladder against Inkwell; win rate where Inkwell was considered

finding.note: True for new deals (win rate 51% to 38%); existing non-promotion churners cite price no more than before

issue_tree.hypothesis: A 12% SMB rise pays for the churn it causes

workplan.analysis: Net ARR at different churn responses; breakeven

finding.note: Only if customers react less than about twice as strongly as in 2023; untested with Inkwell present

issue_tree.label: Economics
issue_tree.hypothesis: A 2027 price rise can deliver 15% ARR growth while keeping NRR above 100%
A 12% rise on every plan adds $10.3M of ARR in 2027

workplan.analysis: Apply renewal shares, enterprise caps and SMB churn to the CFO figure

finding.note: About $7.6M can be repriced in 2027; about $6.3M after SMB churn

issue_tree.hypothesis: Raising only mid-market and enterprise prices reaches 15% growth with NRR above 100%

workplan.analysis: 2027 ARR bridge on trailing NRR plus the segmented rise; NRR by option

finding.note: Adds about $4.3M; needs only $0.6M of new-customer ARR; overall NRR about 114%

issue_tree.label: Low-price SMB plan
issue_tree.hypothesis: A cheaper SMB entry plan would win back deals lost to Inkwell
issue_tree.cut_reason: Out of scope at the brief: new packaging needs cost and cannibalisation data the pack lacks

issue_tree.label: Enterprise caps
issue_tree.hypothesis: Renegotiating enterprise price caps would lift 2027 enterprise ARR
issue_tree.cut_reason: Cannot be moved in 2027: caps are contract terms until each contract renews

issue_tree.label: Usage-based pricing
issue_tree.hypothesis: Charging per document would grow ARR faster than list-price rises
issue_tree.cut_reason: Out of scope for the 2027 plan; no usage or willingness-to-pay data in the pack
